## Narrative

The RaMP enrichment analysis of the 11 differentially-abundant metabolites identifies two overwhelmingly dominant pathways, both carrying an FDR of 0.0 and extraordinary fold-enrichments above 950×: **Galactose Metabolism (KEGG map00052 / SMP00043)** and the disease correlate **Galactosemia (SMP00182)**. Six of the 11 metabolites — galactitol (C01697), myo-inositol (C00137), galactinol (C01235), D-glucose (C00221), sucrose (C00089), and glycerol (C00116) — fall within these related modules, making the galactose / polyol axis the central biological story.

**Driver compounds.** Galactitol (C01697) — a reduced product of galactose via aldose reductase — is annotated in Galactose Metabolism (SMP00043 / map00052) and Galactosemia (SMP00182) with HMDB disease associations that include galactosemia and Alzheimer's disease; tissue enrichment is reported in brain, erythrocytes, and eye lens. Galactinol (C01235) is annotated in Galactose Metabolism and Galactosemia (co-occurrence plausibility 1.0 across all six co-observed metabolites). myo-Inositol (C00137) is annotated across both the Galactose Metabolism (SMP00043 / map00052) and Galactosemia (SMP00182) modules; it additionally appears in Phosphatidylinositol Phosphate Metabolism (map00562) and Inositol Phosphate Metabolism (SMP00462), positioning it as a branch-point between carbohydrate and membrane-lipid pathways.

**Secondary pathway.** The Glycerophospholipid biosynthetic pathway (WP2533, FDR 7.9 × 10⁻⁵) captures myo-inositol, ethanolamine (C00189), and glycerol (C00116), consistent with inositol's role as a precursor for phosphatidylinositol synthesis (KEGG map00562). A separate Reactome module associates dopamine (C03758) with neuronal synaptic pathways, suggesting that neurotransmitter dynamics may be secondarily affected — though this does not reach genome-wide significance relative to the primary carbohydrate signal.

**Biological significance.** The convergence on Galactose Metabolism (map00052 / SMP00043) and Galactosemia (SMP00182) identifies the Leloir pathway and downstream polyol accumulation as the primary metabolic signature. The co-enrichment of myo-inositol across both the carbohydrate and glycerophospholipid modules identifies it as a branch-point metabolite linking sugar metabolism to membrane-lipid biosynthesis.

**Limitations.** Several claims regarding the biochemical role of galactinol and the mechanistic interpretation of the observed enrichments (e.g., treatment-group phenotype, polyol accumulation dynamics) lack direct support in RaMP/KEGG annotation and are framed as testable hypotheses rather than confirmed findings. Experimental follow-up is required to validate directional interpretations.
